summary: Feed s117_double to IDS is degraded: 9.2% duplicate packets and 67.8% encrypted bytes (exceeds 60% IDS tolerance). No packet drops, one-way traffic, VLAN or tool overload issues detected.

findings.root_cause: Duplicate packets from aggregating overlapping SPAN/mirror sessions or dual TAP feeds into one packet broker output without deduplication. 331 of 3605 packets (9.2%) are identical copies seen within a short window.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes cycles analyzing same packet twice, inflates flow/event counts, risks signature misfires and reduces effective inspection capacity for unique traffic.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication on the IDS output to drop identical packets before delivery, restoring accurate traffic volume without losing unique flows.

findings.root_cause: 68% of bytes are encrypted (TLS/QUIC) and forwarded opaque to IDS. IDS needs full payload inspection but tolerates only ~60% encrypted, so most payloads are not inspectable.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS is blind to payload content for majority of traffic, sharply reducing detection coverage for exploits, malware and C2 hidden in encrypted streams.

recommended_fix.why: Decrypt relevant TLS at the visibility layer with proper keys/policy or filter/bypass undecryptable high-entropy traffic so IDS focuses on inspectable traffic; otherwise consider moving IDS behind SSL visibility appliance.
